This script provides an example implementation of the R functions defined in this repository. It loads the cell migration data output from the LapTrack/Cellpose-SAM Python pipeline and uses it to analyse cell migration and plot the results. The data used here have been simulated for the purpose of this example workflow.

## Set up environment

Load packages and specify parameters for the analysis. Ensure that packages have been installed using *install_packages.R* and that functions have been defined by running *define_functions.R*.

```{r, load packages, include=FALSE}
#| echo: false

# specify packages to load
packages <- c('tidyverse', 'readr', 'snakecase','stringr','lme4','RColorBrewer','ggrepel','patchwork','gganimate','factoextra', 'lmerTest', 'bestNormalize', 'car', 'emmeans', 'RNOmni', 'ggsignif')

# load packages
invisible(lapply(packages, library, character.only=TRUE))
```

Now specify parameters for the analysis and load the data.

```{r, specify parameters}
#| echo: false

# data: tracking data output from cell segmentation+tracking script
# experiment plan: experimental design in the format provided
# metadata: imaging metadata in the format provided

data_path             <- "../../data/R_data"
exp_plan_path         <- "../../data/R_data"
metadata_path         <- "../../data/R_data"

# specify treatment condition levels
## NOTE: the order of treatment conditions in treatment_levels_raw and treatment_levels_clean MUST match, otherwise clean_and_normalise_data will return mislabeled data 
treatment_levels_raw <- c("Untreated","VehicleControl","1mg_Dose","2.5mg_Dose","5mg_Dose","10mg_Dose") # these are the labels in the original data

treatment_levels_clean <- c("UT","ctrl","dose_1mg","dose_2.5mg","dose_5mg","dose_10mg") # these are the labels in the desired format

treatment_levels_filt <- c("UT","ctrl","dose_1mg","dose_2.5mg","dose_5mg","dose_10mg") # these are the labels in the desired format, with only the levels of interest (may be the same as _clean if all features are of interest)
```

```{r}
# list names of the experiment plan files, so they can be mapped to experiment names
find_exp_plan_files()
```

```{r, load data files}
# map experiment plan file names to experiment names so they can be assigned correctly 
experiment_by_file <- c(
  "example_exp_1_exp_plan.csv" = "exp_1",
  "example_exp_2_exp_plan.csv" = "exp_2",
  "example_exp_3_exp_plan.csv" = "exp_3"
  )

# load raw data, with experimental information from experiment plan and metadata files
mig_raw <- load_data()
mig_raw
```

If desired, simulated Brownian and correlated random walks can be simulated for comparison to the experimental tracking data.

```{r, simulations}
sim_tracks <- bind_rows(
  # Brownian
  simulate_brownian(),
  # persistent (CRW)
  simulate_crw(label = "Persistent (CRW)"),
  # reduced D (motility)
  simulate_crw(D=0.003 * 0.2, label = "Inhibited Motility"),
  # reduced kappa (persistence)
  simulate_crw(kappa = 0.3, label = "Inhibited Persistence"),
  # reduced D and kappa
  simulate_crw(D=0.003 * 0.2, kappa = 0.3, label = "Inhibited Persistence & Motility")
)

# specify levels for the simulations
sim_tracks$condition <- factor(sim_tracks$condition, levels = c(
  "Brownian",
  "Persistent (CRW)",
  "Inhibited Motility",
  "Inhibited Persistence",
  "Inhibited Persistence & Motility"))

# create global track IDs
sim_tracks <- sim_tracks %>%
  arrange(condition, track_id, frame) %>%
  group_by(global_ID = consecutive_id(condition, track_id))

### the simulated tracks can now be analysed and plotted, then compared to the real tracking data
```

Now clean, normalise, and filter the tracking data.

```{r, pre-process tracking data}
# clean and normalise tracking data
mig_norm <- clean_and_normalise_data()
mig_norm

# filter tracks by length
# NB: no tracks are filtered out here as the simulated tracks are all the expected length
mig_filt <- filter_data(min_length=30)
mig_filt
```

The tracks can be plotted for qualitative comparison of migration across conditions.

```{r, visualise cell tracks}
# plot cell tracks
plot_cell_tracks(conditions=treatment_levels_filt, labels=labels, rows=3)

# make density plots
plot_cell_track_density(conditions=treatment_levels_filt, labels=labels, rows=3)
```

If desired, a subset of the tracks can also be animated into a .gif using gganimate.

```{r, animate tracks}
# this may take a very long time to render, depending on the number of conditions, number of cells, and track length
animate_tracks(conditions=treatment_levels_filt, labels=labels, ntracks=100, rows=3)
```

## Analyse migration features

The tracking dataset is now ready for analysis. Start by analysing per-track (trackwise) measures of displacement and straightness.

```{r, get trackwise migration features}
mig_features <- get_trackwise_features()
mig_features
```

Next, create linear models for each of four key trackwise migration features: total displacement, net displacement, maximum displacement, and meandering index. This will allow for pairwise comparisons between conditions, the significance of which can be shown on boxplots.

```{r, create models for migration feature boxplots}
# create linear model
tot_d_lmm <- get_linear_mixed_model(feature='tot_d')

# check assumptions of the model
check_model_assumptions(linear_model=tot_d_lmm) # model does not meet assumptions

# if the model does not fit well, can try normalising the data to improve normality
# bestNormalize finds the most effective transformation
BN_tot <- bestNormalize(mig_features$tot_d)
BN_tot

# bestNormalize identified orderNorm (inverse-normal) as the best transformation
# NB: because bestNormalize uses repeated cross-validation, it may give slightly different results each time it is run on the same data unless you set.seed first.
#mig_features$tot_d_bc <- predict(BN_tot) # this will apply the transformation identified by bestNormalize
mig_features$tot_d_inv <- RankNorm(mig_features$tot_d) # to apply inverse-normal transformation

# try fitting a model with the transformed data and checking the assumptions
tot_d_transform_lmm <- get_linear_mixed_model(feature='tot_d_inv')
check_model_assumptions(linear_model=tot_d_transform_lmm)
# the model using the transformed data fits much better

# pairs of treatment conditions to compare for the migration feature boxplots
contrasts <- c('ctrl - dose_5mg', 'ctrl - dose_10mg')

# get post-hoc comparisons
tot_d_pairs <- get_posthoc_comparisons(model=tot_d_transform_lmm, contrasts_to_plot = contrasts)
tot_d_pairs$table
```

```{r, get boxplot data for net displacement}
# create linear model
net_d_lmm <- get_linear_mixed_model(feature='net_d')

# check assumptions of the model
check_model_assumptions(linear_model=net_d_lmm) # model does not meet assumptions

# use bestNormalize to identify the most effective transformation
BN_net <- bestNormalize(mig_features$net_d)
BN_net

# bestNormalize did not identify RankNorm (inverse-normal) as best but it is also effective and more commonly used
mig_features$net_d_inv <- RankNorm(mig_features$net_d) # to apply inverse-normal transformation

# try fitting a model with the transformed data and checking the assumptions
net_d_transform_lmm <- get_linear_mixed_model(feature='net_d_inv')
check_model_assumptions(linear_model=net_d_transform_lmm)
# the model using the transformed data fits much better

# get post-hoc comparisons
net_d_pairs <- get_posthoc_comparisons(model=net_d_transform_lmm, contrasts_to_plot = contrasts)
net_d_pairs$table
```

```{r, get boxplot data for maximum displacement}
# create linear model
max_d_lmm <- get_linear_mixed_model(feature='max_d')

# check assumptions of the model
check_model_assumptions(linear_model = max_d_lmm) # model does not meet assumptions

# use bestNormalize to identify the most effective transformation
BN_max <- bestNormalize(mig_features$max_d)
BN_max

# bestNormalize identified orderNorm (inverse-normal) transformation as best
mig_features$max_d_inv <- RankNorm(mig_features$max_d) # to apply inverse-normal transformation

# try fitting a model with the transformed data and checking the assumptions
max_d_transform_lmm <- get_linear_mixed_model(feature='max_d_inv')
check_model_assumptions(linear_model=max_d_transform_lmm)
# the model using the transformed data fits much better

# get post-hoc comparisons
max_d_pairs <- get_posthoc_comparisons(model=max_d_transform_lmm, contrasts_to_plot = contrasts)
max_d_pairs$table
```

```{r, get boxplot data for meandering index}
# create linear model
meand_lmm <- get_linear_mixed_model(feature='meand_index')

# check assumptions of the model
check_model_assumptions(linear_model = meand_lmm) # model does not meet assumptions

# use bestNormalize to identify the most effective transformation
BN_meand <- bestNormalize(mig_features$meand_index)
BN_meand

# bestNormalize did not identify RankNorm (inverse-normal) as best but it is also effective and more commonly used
mig_features$meand_inv <- RankNorm(mig_features$meand_index) # to apply inverse-normal transformation

# try fitting a model with the transformed data and checking the assumptions
meand_transform_lmm <- get_linear_mixed_model(feature='meand_inv')
check_model_assumptions(linear_model=meand_transform_lmm)
# the model using the transformed data fits much better

# get post-hoc comparisons
meand_pairs <- get_posthoc_comparisons(model=meand_transform_lmm, contrasts_to_plot = contrasts)
meand_pairs$table
```

Now that the linear models have been created for each feature, create the boxplots and the 4-feature figure panel.

```{r}
# specify readable labels for the plots (if not already the same as treatment_levels_filt)
labels = c(UT = "Untreated",
           ctrl = "(-)",
           dose_1mg = "1mg",
           dose_2.5mg = "2.5mg",
           dose_5mg = "5mg",
           dose_10mg = "10mg")

# total displacement
tot_d_plot <- make_feature_boxplot(model=tot_d_transform_lmm, data=mig_features, labels=labels,
                                      feature='tot_d_inv', title='Total Displacement', 
                                      y_label='Inverse-normal transformed total displacement (µm)',
                                      contrasts_to_plot = contrasts)

# net displacement
net_d_plot <- make_feature_boxplot(model=net_d_transform_lmm, data=mig_features, labels=labels,
                                      feature='net_d_inv', title='Net Displacement', 
                                      y_label='Inverse-normal transformed net displacement (µm)',
                                      contrasts_to_plot = contrasts)

# maximum displacement
max_d_plot <- make_feature_boxplot(model=max_d_transform_lmm, data=mig_features, labels=labels,
                                      feature='max_d_inv', title='Maximum Displacement', 
                                      y_label='Inverse-normal transformed maximum displacement (µm)',
                                      contrasts_to_plot = contrasts)

# meandering index
meand_plot <- make_feature_boxplot(model=meand_transform_lmm, data=mig_features, labels=labels,
                                      feature='meand_inv', title='Meandering Index', 
                                      y_label='Inverse-normal transformed meandering index',
                                      contrasts_to_plot = contrasts)

# assemble the plots into a 4-panel composite figure
make_migration_boxplot_figure()
```

## MSD modelling

Next perform ensemble lag-time mean-squared displacement modelling to compare the diffusivity of cells in each treatment condition to Brownian motion.

```{r, MSD modelling}
# get MSD for each track (this may take some time)
msd_per_track <- get_msd_per_track()

# compute ensemble lag-time MSD for all cells in a treatment condition
msd_ensemble <- get_ensemble_msd()

# then extract the model coefficients (D and alpha) for each condition
model_coeffs <- ensemble_msd_fit()
model_coeffs

# repeat for each experiment seperately
# so that we can get the error for each coefficient (D and alpha)
msd_ensemble_by_experiment <- get_ensemble_msd_by_experiment()
model_coeffs_by_experiment <- ensemble_MSD_fit_by_experiment()
alpha_summ_stats <- summarise_alpha()
alpha_summ_stats

# summarise the MSD model coefficients and previously computed migration features
mig_features_summ <- summarise_migration_features(msd_coeffs = model_coeffs_by_experiment)
mig_features_summ
```

The MSD vs lag time and anomalous diffusion exponent can be plotted seperately and combined into a figure panel.

```{r, visualise MSD and alpha}
plot_MSD_vs_lag_time(palette='sequential', labels=labels)
plot_alpha(labels=labels)
  
plot_alpha_and_msd_panel(palette='sequential', labels=labels)
```

Finally, a PCA can be constructed for dimensionality reduction using both the migration feature data and the MSD model coefficients.

```{r, PCA with MSD coeffs}
# construct PCA
pca_results <- get_pca()

# understand explained variance
plot_pca_scree()

# understand which features contribute to each PC
plot_pca_contribution(axis=1) # PC1
plot_pca_contribution(axis=2) # PC2
plot_pca_biplot_variables()

# visualise samples relative to the PCs
plot_pca_scatter(palette='sequential', labels=labels)
```

If preferred, a PCA can be constructed using all trackwise features (excluding D and alpha, as they are modelled per-experiment).

```{r, PCA with just trackwise migration features}
# construct PCA
pca_results <- get_pca(data=mig_features,
                       features=c('net_d','tot_d','max_d','meand_index'))

# understand explained variance
plot_pca_scree()

# understand which features contribute to each PC
plot_pca_contribution(axis=1) # PC1
plot_pca_contribution(axis=2) # PC2
plot_pca_biplot_variables()

# visualise samples relative to the PCs
plot_pca_scatter(palette='sequential', labels=labels, name='PCA_scatter_mig_features.png')
```
